stemMarkdown: If the polynomial $p(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6$ is divided by $(x-3)$, what is the remainder?
solutionMarkdown:
We can use the Remainder Theorem. According to it, if a polynomial $p(x)$ is divided by $(x - c)$, then the remainder of this division is $p(c)$. Here, $c = 3$, so we need to evaluate $p(3)$:

$$
p(3) = 3^3 - 6 \cdot 3^2 + 11 \cdot 3 - 6 = 27 - 54 + 33 - 6 = 0.
$$
Thus, the remainder when $p(x)$ is divided by $(x-3)$ is \(0\).
